scenario: Which Zero Trust principle says every access request should be fully authenticated and authorized using all available signals?

options.note: Limits blast radius and uses analytics.

explanation: 'Verify explicitly' means every access request is fully authenticated and authorized using all available signals: identity, location, device health, service or workload, data classification and anomalies. Trusting the corporate network is exactly what Zero Trust rejects, and 'least privilege' and 'assume breach' are separate principles.

refs.title: Describe security and compliance concepts: Describe the Zero Trust model
Zero Trust as a security foundation

scenario: Which Zero Trust principle recommends segmenting access and using end-to-end encryption to limit damage from an attack?

options.note: A layered strategy, not a Zero Trust principle.

explanation: 'Assume breach' means designing as though attackers are already inside: segment access by network, user, device and app, encrypt end to end, and use analytics to detect threats and limit blast radius. The three Zero Trust principles are verify explicitly, use least privilege access, and assume breach. Defense in depth is a separate concept.

refs.title: Describe security and compliance concepts: Describe the Zero Trust model
Zero Trust as a security foundation

scenario: Which Zero Trust principle is applied by giving just-in-time and just-enough access?
explanation: Just-in-time and just-enough access (JIT/JEA) are how you apply 'use least privilege access', along with risk-based adaptive policies and data protection. Users get only the access they need, only when they need it.

refs.title: Describe security and compliance concepts: Describe the Zero Trust model
Zero Trust as a security foundation

scenario: In the shared responsibility model, which responsibility always stays with the customer, whatever the cloud service type?

options.note: The cloud provider's in IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.

explanation: Information and data, devices, and accounts and identities are always the customer's responsibility in any deployment, from on-premises to SaaS. The physical hosts, physical network and physical datacenter are always Microsoft's in the cloud.

refs.title: Describe security and compliance concepts: Describe the shared responsibility model
Shared responsibility in the cloud - Microsoft Azure

scenario: In which cloud model does the customer have the MOST responsibility?

options.text: Responsibility is equal in all models

explanation: With IaaS, the customer is responsible for the most: OS, network controls, applications and data. In PaaS the provider takes more, and in SaaS the customer's responsibility shrinks to data, identities, devices and settings.

refs.title: Describe security and compliance concepts: Describe the shared responsibility model
Shared responsibility in the cloud - Microsoft Azure

scenario: What is defense in depth?

options.text: Using multiple layers of security controls
Relying on one strong perimeter firewall for everything
Trusting all users once they're on the internal network

explanation: Defense in depth protects data with multiple layers of security controls (physical, identity and access, perimeter, network, compute, application, data). If an attacker defeats one layer, the next still protects the data. One perimeter firewall, or trusting everyone on the internal network, is the single-layer thinking it replaces.

refs.title: Describe security and compliance concepts: Describe defense in depth

scenario: Which part of the CIA triad ensures data hasn't been changed by unauthorized people?
explanation: Integrity means data hasn't been altered by unauthorized parties. Confidentiality is about keeping data secret, availability is about it being accessible when needed, and authentication isn't part of the CIA triad. Hashing and digital signatures are common ways to verify integrity.

refs.title: Describe concepts of cryptography: Describe hashing and its application in digital signing

scenario: Which process converts data into an unreadable form that can be reversed with a key?
explanation: Encryption converts readable data into ciphertext that can be reversed with the right key. Hashing is one-way and can't be reversed. Symmetric encryption uses one key, while asymmetric encryption uses a public and private key pair.

refs.title: Describe security and compliance concepts: Describe encryption and hashing
Describe concepts of cryptography: Describe encryption and its use in cybersecurity

scenario: Why are passwords stored as salted hashes rather than encrypted?

options.text: Hashes can't be reversed to reveal the password
Hashes are faster for the server to decrypt later
Encryption is not allowed for password storage

explanation: Passwords are stored as salted hashes because a hash is one-way: even if the database leaks, the passwords can't be reversed from it. The server hashes what the user types and compares. A salt makes identical passwords produce different hashes, which defeats precomputed rainbow tables. If passwords were encrypted, anyone with the key could read them all.

refs.title: Describe security and compliance concepts: Describe encryption and hashing
Describe concepts of cryptography: Describe hashing and its application in digital signing

scenario: What's the difference between authentication and authorization?

options.text: Authentication proves identity; authorization grants access
Authentication decides which permissions a user gets

explanation: Authentication proves who you are; authorization determines what you're allowed to do. Authentication comes first, and authorization uses the verified identity to grant permissions. Treating them as one thing, or reversing them, is the common exam trap.

refs.title: Describe identity concepts: Define authentication and authorization

scenario: Which term describes rules from governments or industry that organizations must follow for data?

options.note: One aspect: where data is stored.

options.text: Encryption at rest for all data

explanation: Regulatory compliance means following the laws and regulations governments or industry bodies set for how data is handled, such as GDPR or HIPAA. Data residency and encryption are individual controls, and Zero Trust is a security model, not a rulebook.

refs.title: Describe security and compliance concepts: Describe governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) concepts

scenario: What is data sovereignty?

options.text: Data is subject to the laws of the country where it's collected or stored
Data must always be encrypted when stored anywhere
Data stored in the cloud becomes the provider's property
Data can never leave the device

explanation: Data sovereignty means data is subject to the laws of the country or region where it's collected or stored. Data residency is the narrower question of where it is physically stored. Encryption and ownership are different questions.

refs.title: Describe security and compliance concepts: Describe governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) concepts

scenario: Which describes an identity provider (IdP)?

options.text: A service that authenticates users and issues tokens
A firewall that blocks unauthorized network traffic
A central database that stores shared files

explanation: An identity provider authenticates users and issues security tokens (using OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0 or SAML) that applications trust. Microsoft Entra ID is an identity provider. A firewall, file store or backup service doesn't issue tokens.

refs.title: Describe identity concepts: Describe the role of the identity provider

scenario: What is Microsoft Entra ID?

options.text: A cloud-based identity and access management service
An on-premises Windows Server domain controller
An antivirus product for Windows devices

explanation: Microsoft Entra ID, formerly Azure Active Directory, is Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service, providing sign-in, SSO, MFA and conditional access to apps. It isn't an on-premises domain controller, antivirus or data classification tool.

refs.title: Describe the function and identity types of Microsoft Entra ID: Describe Microsoft Entra ID
What is Microsoft Entra?

scenario: Which feature lets users reset their own forgotten password without calling the help desk?
explanation: Self-service password reset lets users reset or unlock their own accounts without calling the help desk, after registering authentication methods first. PIM, Conditional Access and access reviews don't reset passwords.

refs.title: Describe the authentication capabilities of Microsoft Entra ID: Describe self-service password reset
Self-service password reset deep dive

scenario: Which Entra feature evaluates signals like user, location and device to allow, block or require MFA?
explanation: Conditional Access combines signals (user, location, device, application, risk) in 'if-then' policies, then allows, blocks or requires controls such as MFA. Entra Connect, access packages and password protection don't make access decisions from signals.

refs.title: Describe access management capabilities of Microsoft Entra: Describe Conditional Access
Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine

scenario: Which authentication method is passwordless?

options.text: A FIDO2 security key or passkey
A password plus a one-time SMS code
Security questions answered at each sign-in

explanation: A FIDO2 security key or passkey is passwordless: no password is involved at all. A password plus SMS code is still MFA built on a password. Windows Hello for Business and Microsoft Authenticator are other passwordless options.

refs.title: Describe the authentication capabilities of Microsoft Entra ID: Describe authentication methods
Passkeys (FIDO2) authentication method in Microsoft Entra ID

scenario: Which MFA method is considered the least secure?

options.text: Microsoft Authenticator push with number matching

explanation: SMS codes are the weakest MFA option because messages can be intercepted or redirected through SIM swapping. FIDO2 keys, Windows Hello for Business and Authenticator with number matching resist phishing and interception better.

refs.title: Describe the authentication capabilities of Microsoft Entra ID: Describe authentication methods
Microsoft Entra authentication overview

scenario: Which service provides just-in-time, time-limited activation of administrator roles?
explanation: Privileged Identity Management provides just-in-time, time-limited activation of admin roles, with optional approval, MFA and justification, and it logs every activation. ID Protection detects risk, SSPR resets passwords, and Entra Connect Sync syncs identities.

refs.title: Describe the identity protection and governance capabilities of Microsoft Entra: Describe the capabilities of Privileged Identity Management
What is Privileged Identity Management?

scenario: Which service detects risky sign-ins, such as leaked credentials or impossible travel?
explanation: Microsoft Entra ID Protection detects risky sign-ins and risky users, such as leaked credentials or impossible travel, and feeds risk levels into Conditional Access so you can require MFA or a password change. Purview, Firewall and Defender for Cloud Apps don't evaluate identity risk this way.

refs.title: Describe the identity protection and governance capabilities of Microsoft Entra: Describe Microsoft Entra ID Protection
What is Microsoft Entra ID Protection?

scenario: Which Entra ID Governance feature lets managers regularly confirm whether users still need access?
explanation: Access reviews let managers or owners regularly confirm whether users still need access to groups, apps and roles, so stale access gets removed. Conditional Access, password protection and Entra Connect don't recertify access.

refs.title: Describe the identity protection and governance capabilities of Microsoft Entra: Describe access reviews

scenario: Which feature bundles groups, apps and sites so users can request access in one step?
explanation: Entitlement management access packages bundle groups, apps and SharePoint sites so a user can request everything for a role in one step, with approvals and expiration. Administrative units, dynamic groups and security defaults don't package access.

refs.title: Describe the identity protection and governance capabilities of Microsoft Entra: Describe access reviews
What is entitlement management?

scenario: Which tool synchronizes on-premises Active Directory users to Microsoft Entra ID?
explanation: Microsoft Entra Connect (or Cloud Sync) synchronizes on-premises Active Directory identities to Microsoft Entra ID, creating hybrid identity. Entra Domain Services provides managed domain services, and Intune and Bastion are unrelated.

scenario: Which hybrid authentication option stores a hash of the on-premises password hash in the cloud?

options.note: Uses an external IdP like AD FS.

explanation: Password hash synchronization stores a hash of the on-premises password hash in the cloud, so users sign in to Entra ID with the same password. It's the simplest hybrid option and also enables leaked credential detection. Pass-through authentication validates against on-premises AD, and federation uses an external identity provider.

scenario: A company wants partner employees to sign in to its apps using their own work accounts. Which feature fits?
explanation: Entra External ID B2B collaboration lets partner employees sign in to your apps with their own work accounts as guests, authenticating through their home identity provider. You avoid creating and managing local accounts for them.

scenario: Which identity type should an Azure app use to access Key Vault without storing credentials in code?
explanation: A managed identity is an automatically managed service principal in Entra ID. An Azure app uses it to get tokens for services such as Key Vault, so no credentials are stored in code or configuration. Shared user accounts or admin accounts would mean secrets to manage.

scenario: Which Entra feature blocks users from setting commonly used weak passwords?

options.note: Lets users reset passwords; it does not ban weak ones.

explanation: Microsoft Entra Password Protection blocks weak and commonly used passwords using a global banned list, plus an optional custom banned list you maintain. Conditional Access, SSPR and PIM don't evaluate password strength.

scenario: What are security defaults in Microsoft Entra ID?

options.text: Preconfigured baseline settings like requiring MFA
Default Azure Firewall rules for all VNets

explanation: Security defaults are preconfigured baseline protections in Entra ID, free of charge, including requiring MFA registration for all users and for admins. They suit organizations that don't use Conditional Access. They aren't custom policies, firewall rules or labels.

scenario: What is a device's state when it's registered to Entra ID but owned by the user (BYOD)?

refs.title: What is device identity in Microsoft Entra ID?

scenario: Which Entra ID role type controls who can manage Entra ID itself, such as creating users?
explanation: Microsoft Entra roles (such as User Administrator or Global Administrator) control who can manage Entra ID itself, for example creating users. Azure RBAC roles (Owner, Contributor, Reader) control access to Azure resources instead.

scenario: Which Microsoft product provides secure access to internal apps and the internet as part of Global Secure Access?

Private Access secures access to internal apps and Internet Access secures traffic to the internet and Microsoft 365. DDoS, DLP and Cloud Apps do other jobs.

scenario: Which protocol is commonly used for modern app authorization, letting apps access APIs for a user?
explanation: OAuth 2.0 is the standard for delegated authorization: it lets an app access an API on a user's behalf. OpenID Connect adds authentication on top of it, and SAML is a common protocol for enterprise SSO. NTLM, Kerberos and SMTP aren't modern app authorization protocols.

scenario: Which feature gives users one sign-in for many applications?
explanation: Single sign-on lets a user sign in once and access many applications, reducing password fatigue and reuse. MFA, password expiration and account lockout are different controls.

scenario: Which logs show who signed in to Entra ID, from where, and whether it succeeded?
explanation: Sign-in logs record who signed in, from where, with which app, and whether it succeeded or what Conditional Access did. Audit logs record changes such as adding users or changing roles, and provisioning logs track app provisioning.

scenario: Which Entra ID Governance feature automates tasks when employees join, move or leave?
explanation: Lifecycle workflows in Entra ID Governance automate joiner, mover and leaver tasks, such as sending a welcome email or removing access on the last day. Conditional Access, password protection and security defaults aren't lifecycle tools.

scenario: What does Microsoft Entra Verified ID provide?

options.text: Digital credentials that users can share and others verify

explanation: Microsoft Entra Verified ID issues and verifies digital credentials (decentralized identity based on open standards). Users hold credentials that others can verify, for example proof of employment. It isn't antivirus, firewalling or email encryption.

refs.title: Describe the identity protection and governance capabilities of Microsoft Entra: Describe Microsoft Entra Verified ID
Introduction to Microsoft Entra Verified ID

scenario: Which group type adds members automatically based on user attributes like department?

options.note: Membership is assigned unless set to dynamic.

explanation: A dynamic membership group adds and removes members automatically based on user or device attributes, such as department. Assigned groups need manual membership, and administrative units delegate administration. Dynamic groups require Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher.

scenario: Which license tier is needed for risk-based Conditional Access with Entra ID Protection?
explanation: Risk-based Conditional Access uses sign-in and user risk from Entra ID Protection, which requires Microsoft Entra ID P2. P1 gives Conditional Access without risk signals, and Free has neither. P2 also includes Privileged Identity Management.

scenario: Which Azure service protects resources from distributed denial-of-service attacks with adaptive tuning and attack analytics?
explanation: Azure DDoS Protection defends against distributed denial-of-service attacks, with adaptive tuning, attack analytics and telemetry, and support. Basic infrastructure protection is automatic for all of Azure; the Network Protection tier adds tuning, alerts and rapid response support.

scenario: Which managed, stateful firewall service filters traffic across Azure virtual networks with threat intelligence?

options.note: Basic allow/deny rules per subnet or NIC.

explanation: Azure Firewall is a managed, cloud-based, stateful firewall that filters traffic across virtual networks, with threat intelligence-based filtering and FQDN rules, centrally managed with policies. NSGs filter at the subnet or NIC level and aren't a managed firewall service.

refs.title: Describe core infrastructure security services in Azure: Describe Azure Firewall

scenario: Which service lets admins connect to VMs over RDP or SSH through the Azure portal without public IP addresses?
explanation: Azure Bastion gives secure RDP/SSH to VMs directly from the Azure portal over TLS, so the VMs need no public IP addresses and no exposed management ports. Azure Firewall, DDoS Protection and Key Vault don't provide remote access.

refs.title: Describe core infrastructure security services in Azure: Describe Azure Bastion

scenario: Which Azure feature filters traffic to and from resources in a subnet using allow and deny rules?
explanation: Network security groups filter network traffic to and from Azure resources using allow and deny rules based on source, destination, port and protocol, processed by priority. Policy, Sentinel and Defender for Office 365 aren't traffic filters.

scenario: Which service protects web apps from attacks like SQL injection and cross-site scripting?
explanation: A web application firewall protects web apps from common exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. It runs on Application Gateway, Front Door and Azure CDN. NSGs filter at the network layer and don't understand HTTP attacks.

refs.title: Describe core infrastructure security services in Azure: Describe Web Application Firewall

scenario: Which service securely stores secrets, keys and certificates?
explanation: Azure Key Vault securely stores and controls access to secrets, keys and certificates, and logs access. Blob Storage isn't designed to protect secrets, and Sentinel and Bastion do other jobs.

refs.title: Azure Key Vault overview

scenario: Which Microsoft service is a cloud-native SIEM and SOAR solution?
explanation: Microsoft Sentinel is a cloud-native SIEM and SOAR solution: it collects data at scale, detects threats, investigates incidents and automates responses. Defender for Cloud is posture management and workload protection, and Purview and Intune are not SIEMs.

Security operations analytics reporting; builds reports
System of audit records; stores logs
Secure online access routing; routes user traffic

options.text: A unified suite correlating threats across endpoints, identities, email and apps
A next-generation network firewall for Azure VNets
A password manager for Microsoft 365 users

scenario: Which service is Microsoft's cloud access security broker (CASB) for discovering and controlling SaaS apps?

Hunting for threats in security logs

explanation: Just-in-time VM access in Defender for Cloud locks down inbound management ports such as RDP and SSH, and opens them only when requested, for a limited time and from approved addresses. PIM and access reviews govern roles, not network ports.

scenario: Which statement about Azure network security groups is true?

options.text: Rules are processed in priority order

explanation: NSG rules are processed in priority order: lower numbers have higher priority, and processing stops at the first matching rule. NSGs filter on source, destination, port and protocol; they don't inspect application payloads or encrypt traffic, and they can deny.

scenario: Which describes the difference between retention labels and retention policies?

options.text: Labels apply to items; policies apply to locations
Policies encrypt content; labels only add headers
Labels block email; policies block file sharing

explanation: Retention policies are applied to locations (for example all mailboxes or a SharePoint site), while retention labels are applied to individual items such as a document or email, by users or automatically. They aren't the same thing, and neither encrypts content.

scenario: Which privacy principle does Microsoft follow regarding customer data?
explanation: Microsoft's privacy principles say customers control their data, with transparency about how it's used, strong security, strong legal protections, and no content-based targeting. Microsoft doesn't sell customer data or use it for ads.

scenario: A company must keep financial records for seven years so they can't be changed. Which feature fits?
